papers.title: Certified pandigital approximations of $\pi$, $\gamma$, $\delta$ and $e$
papers.abstract: In 2004 Erich Friedman asked for the best approximations of $\pi$, $e$, the Euler-Mascheroni constant $\gamma$ and Feigenbaum's constant $\delta$ that use each of the digits $1,\dots,n$ exactly once, with addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, exponentiation, parentheses and the decimal point. We determine the optimal expressions for $\pi$, $\gamma$ and $\delta$ for every $n \le 9$, with the digits in any order and in increasing order, and for $e$ when $n \le 6$. The optima are found by exhaustive search and certified by an independent algorithm that encloses every expression rigorously and decides each candidate with Arb and exact arithmetic; a second certified computation covers intermediate values of any size. Twenty-one entries improve the published records; for $\pi$ with the digits 1-9 the optimal error is $2.81\cdot 10^{-14}$. For $e$, whose records come from identities between power towers, we prove that Bamberger's formula is optimal within the natural family of such identities. All code and certificates are public.

papers.title: On the ring of bounded functions on the character variety
papers.abstract: Let $\mathfrak{X}$ denote the character variety associated to the group $(o_L, +)$, where $o_L$ is the ring of integers in a finite extension $L/\mathbb{Q}_p$. $\mathfrak{X}$ is a rigid analytic variety parametrizing locally $L$-analytic characters. Let $\Lambda_L\left(\mathfrak{X}\right)$ denote the global sections bounded by $1$. In this paper we prove that $\Lambda_L\left(\mathfrak{X}\right)= o_L[[o_L]]$, answering the question posed in [AB24].

papers.title: A Hopf algebra action on the cohomology of moduli of abelian varieties
papers.abstract: We show that the rational compactly supported cohomology of the moduli space $\mathcal{A} = \bigsqcup_{g \geq 0} \mathcal{A}_g$ of principally polarized abelian varieties is free as a bigraded module over the Hopf algebra formed by its weight-zero subspace. The action arises from a symplectic analog of the Waldhausen $S$-construction. This structure yields new lower bounds for Betti numbers and the dimensions of the graded pieces of the weight filtration on the cohomology of $\mathcal{A}_g$. In particular, $\dim H_c^{2g + k}(\mathcal{A}_g)$ grows at least exponentially with $g$ for every nonnegative $k \neq 1, 3$. We also give conjectural descriptions of the full mixed Hodge structures in genera four and five, and of mixed Tate subquotients of $H_c^{2g}(\mathcal{A}_g)$ associated with shuffle algebras and multiple zeta values in every genus.

papers.title: Moduli spaces of $(3,6)$-$K3$ surfaces and cubic surfaces
papers.abstract: We compare the ball quotient for marked nodal cubic surfaces with the arithmetic quotient of a domain of type IV associated with $K3$ surfaces arising from configurations of six lines in $\mathbb{P}^2$. Using the Coble map and the period mapping associated with the hypergeometric system of type $(3,6)$, we identify a common open subset of the GIT quotient of six ordered points in $\mathbb{P}^2$ and the ball quotient. This identification gives an analog in dimension four of the Janus-like phenomenon for the Segre cubic and the Igusa quartic, making precise a comparison suggested by Allcock, Carlson, and Toledo. For a related family of lattice-polarized $K3$ surfaces, we give a geometric realization of the ring of meromorphic modular forms with prescribed poles and trivial character and describe the corresponding Looijenga compactification.

papers.title: The rational points of the non-split Cartan modular curve of level 121
papers.abstract: We prove that the modular curve $X_{\mathrm{ns}}^{+}(121)$ of the normalizer of a non-split Cartan subgroup of level 121, of genus 511, has exactly seven rational points, all of them CM. This is the level 121 case of a conjecture of Rouse, Sutherland and Zureick-Brown, and with their theorem it determines the 11-adic images of Galois of non-CM elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$. The Jacobian has rank equal to the genus. At $p = 17$ and $43$ one Hecke block of the Mordell-Weil group has logarithm divisible by $p^2$ but $p$-adic height of valuation one, and a comparison of valuations in the quadratic Chabauty identity then shows that each CM point is the only rational point in its residue disc, with no computation of the local height at $p$, no basis of the Mordell-Weil group and no equations for the curve. The inputs come from expansions of differentials at CM points and from a formula we prove for intersection numbers of CM divisors of coprime fundamental discriminants under Hecke operators on $X_{\mathrm{ns}}^{+}(\ell^e)$ (Theorem 1.3).

papers.title: Rational Elliptic Period Relations Across Realizations: Complex Lattices, Local p-adic Periods, and Drinfeld Modules
papers.abstract: We determine the algebraic relations among full de Rham comparison periods of elliptic curves over finite extensions of $\mathbb Q_p$. The connected local monodromy group gives the transcendence degree and an explicit affine linear relation ideal for the full matrix in Fontaine's field $B_{\mathrm{dR}}$. After normalizing the holomorphic row and reducing to $\mathbb C_p$, the transcendence degree drops by one and the normalized determinant supplies the additional relation. Every polynomial relation of degree at most $d$ is detected modulo $t^{d+1}$. For $d\ge1$ this bound is sharp for each elliptic curve. A rational quasi-period row gives a Galois-stable Tate line. Together with an algebraic holomorphic period ratio it forces potential splitting, which identifies the exact ordinary CM obstruction. We compute the full Tate matrix. For ordinary non-CM curves with $p\ge5$, the standard quasi-period row is rational precisely at a zero of Katz's $E_{2,p}$. Away from the zeros the two full ratios are algebraically independent. At the zeros, a nonzero quasi-period and the normalized holomorphic ratio have algebraically independent images in $\mathbb C_p$. The complex question that motivates these results, the analogue for Drinfeld modules, and a conditional arithmetic consequence for Katz values complete the comparison.

papers.title: Equivariant iterated Eisenstein integrals for congruence subgroups of level 2
papers.abstract: The modular properties of holomorphic Eisenstein series for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ and its congruence subgroups do not carry over to their primitives. Instead, the transformation of iterated Eisenstein integrals under congruence subgroups of level $N$ introduces inhomogeneous terms comprising (among others) cyclotomic multiple zeta values of level $N$. We combine iterated Eisenstein integrals for the congruence subgroups of level $N=2$ of arbitrary iteration depth with their complex conjugates and (single-valued) level-2 cyclotomic multiple zeta values such that they define non-holomorphic modular forms. Our construction of these so-called equivariant iterated Eisenstein integrals for $\Gamma(2)$ and $\Gamma_0(2)$ proceeds at the level of generating series that take values in an infinite-dimensional (pro-unipotent) Lie group and closely follow Brown's analogous construction in the $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ case. The required insertions of cyclotomic multiple zeta values are controlled by zeta generators for level 2 that normalise the corresponding (pro-nilpotent) Lie algebra of the generating series and whose Lie-bracket relations we determine systematically. Upon restriction to Eisenstein series of modular weight~2, we recover single-valued multiple polylogarithms on the genus 0 modular curve $\Gamma(2)\backslash \mathbb{H}$.

papers.title: Unlikely intersections in Shimura varieties and beyond: a survey
papers.abstract: The aim of this note is to provide a concise introduction to so-called problems of unlikely intersections for (pure) Shimura varieties and to review the current state-of-the-art. In the process, we will touch upon more general settings and some of the results in those contexts.

papers.title: Millicharged particles and the degree-3 Prouhet-Tarry-Escott problem
papers.abstract: We use geometry to solve a problem in arithmetic relevant for physics. Namely, for any $m$ we find all integer solutions to the equations $\sum_{i=1}^m x_i^k = \sum_{i=1}^m y_i^k$, where $k \in \{1,2,3\}$; this seems to be new for $m \geq 5$. In physics, these are the anomaly cancellation conditions for models with $m$ fermions which can be naturally light and carry small electric charges (a.k.a. millicharged or minicharged particles). The small charges arise by kinetic mixing of the Standard Model $U(1)$ gauge symmetry with an unbroken non-chiral (a.k.a. vector-like) $U(1)$ and the masses are suppressed by a spontaneously-broken chiral $U(1)$.

papers.title: On the Erd\H{o}s--Ginzburg--Ziv problem for $\mathbb Z_n^3$
papers.abstract: The Erd\H{o}s--Ginzburg--Ziv constant $\mathsf s(\mathbb Z_n^r)$ is the least positive integer $t$ such that every sequence of $t$ elements of $\mathbb Z_n^r$ contains $n$ terms whose sum is zero. In this paper, we prove that $$\mathsf s(\mathbb Z_n^3)=9n+o(n)$$ for odd $n$. For every fixed $r\ge 4$, we also show that $\mathsf s(\mathbb Z_n^r)\le\bigl(\binom{2r-1}{r}+1\bigr)n+o_r(n).$ Our approach combines Alon--Dubiner-type spectral expansion, Zakharov's convex-geometric framework, and restricted-sum ideas developed by Han and Ren.

papers.title: Comodule algebras and the cohomology of symplectic groups
papers.abstract: We prove that the homology of symplectic groups with Steinberg module coefficients forms a comodule algebra over the homology of general linear groups with Steinberg module coefficients. We prove a freeness-type result for comodule algebras. We deduce new lower bounds for the high-dimensional cohomology of symplectic groups of number rings and their congruence subgroups.

papers.title: The Semi--Fibonacci Partition Tree
papers.abstract: In this work, we introduce a binary tree in which every semi-Fibonacci partition appears exactly once. The left--right address of a vertex gives an explicit formula for the parts of the corresponding partition and encodes statistics such as the largest $2$-adic valuation among its parts. We construct a sign-reversing involution that refines Andrews's parity theorem by determining the difference between the numbers of partitions of a given integer at even and odd depths. Inspired by properties of the Calkin--Wilf tree, we study several parameters of our tree and use them to obtain new results on semi-Fibonacci partitions. We also derive generating functions for partition statistics and determine the average and extremal partition sizes at each level.

papers.title: Rational Designs and Prouhet--Tarry--Escott Problems
papers.abstract: For every strength, we prove the existence of rational designs on spheres, orthogonal and unitary groups, real and complex Grassmannians, and ellipsoids that are defined by positive-definite quadratic forms with rational coefficients and have a rational point. This answers Bannai's Problem for these spaces, solves the problem of Cui--Xia--Xiang on rational spherical $4$-designs on the unit circle, and proves Xiang's conjecture in the stronger form of existence in every dimension. To this end, we introduce the $(G,\mathcal{S})$-Prouhet--Tarry--Escott problem for an abelian group $G$ and a finite set of characters $\mathcal{S}$ and develop its existence and minimality theory. We also prove a general theorem transforming integer-weighted rational designs into equi-weighted designs on distinct rational points. On the unit circle $\mathbb{S}^1$, we determine the minimum sizes of rational spherical designs of strengths $4,5,6,7$ and show that they are respectively $2304,4608,9216,9216$. We also show that the minimum size of a rational spherical $5$-design on $\mathbb{S}^2$ is $192$. We further apply our framework to prove a conjecture of Thuswaldner--Ziegler on sums of distinct units and to answer Mahabaduge's problem on convex equilateral lattice polygons affirmatively.

papers.title: A sharp bounded bijection for tight cylindric partitions
papers.abstract: Fix a cyclic profile of coprime rank $r$ and level $\ell$, both at least three, and an entry bound $n\ge1$. Let $d$ be the deficit from the maximum volume of a tight cylindric partition. For $d\le n\min(r,\ell)$, the one-row combinatorial $R$ matches the tight cylinders whose last slice lies inside the maximizer's last slice with the partitions of $d$ in which each part occurs fewer than $r$ times. The inverse preserves the profile and entry bound. We identify every partition missed at the next deficit. A prefix test decides whether any cylinder lies outside this sector and, if so, identifies the unique one of least deficit. This explains the leading coefficient gap in Warnaar's $Q_{n,c}$. We also determine the first correction to the vertex terms of the published bounded determinant.

papers.title: Fourier bases for square-order Paley graphs
papers.abstract: Let $q$ be an odd prime power and consider the Paley graph $P(q^2)$ on the finite field $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$. A well-known optimal eigenfunction of this graph is supported on the norm-one subgroup, where it takes the values $1$ and $-1$ on the two cosets of its subgroup of index two. Its support has the minimum possible size $q+1$. Starting from this eigenfunction, we construct a family of multiplicative translates and prove that they form a basis of the space of complex-valued functions on $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}^{\times}$. After extending these functions to the whole field, the translates indexed by squares form a basis of one nonprincipal eigenspace of the Paley graph, while those indexed by nonsquares form a basis of the other. In particular, both nonprincipal eigenspaces admit bases consisting entirely of optimal eigenfunctions. The main ingredient is a multiplicative Fourier analysis of the shifted eigenfunction. We determine the moduli of all its Fourier coefficients and, in particular, show that none of them vanishes.

papers.title: Quasipolynomial pyjamas
papers.abstract: The ``pyjama stripe" $E(\varepsilon)$ is the set of all complex numbers whose real part lies within $\varepsilon$ of the nearest integer. The Pyjama Problem asks whether, for each $\varepsilon > 0$, there exists some union of finitely many rotations of $E(\varepsilon)$ about the origin that covers the plane. This was answered in the affirmative by Manners. Kravitz and Leng subsequently showed that $\exp(\exp(\exp(\varepsilon^{-O(1)})))$ rotations suffice. In this paper, we prove an upper bound of \[\exp((\log \varepsilon^{-1})^{50000})\] rotations. We also show that at least $(\pi/2 + 0.003 + o(1))\varepsilon^{-1}$ rotations are necessary, improving upon the natural lower bound of $(\pi/2 + o(1))\varepsilon^{-1}$.

papers.title: Orbits of $p$-adic flows: balls, time-one maps and minimal group actions
papers.abstract: Let $f$ be a vector field on $\mathbb{Z}_p^d$ given by polynomials, or by power series converging on $\mathbb{Z}_p^d$, whose coefficients are divisible by $p^c$, where $c \ge 1$ ($c \ge 2$ when $p = 2$). Its flow exists for every $p$-adic time. I show that $t \mapsto \varphi_t(x)$ multiplies distances by exactly $\|f(x)\|_p$, in every dimension. This gives explicit flow-box coordinates, closed formulas for hitting times, return times and orbit averages, and a Newton iteration that computes them with quadratic convergence; in dimension one it recovers Mukhamedov's theorem that interpolated orbits are balls. I then show that the analytic maps $g$ congruent to the identity modulo $p^c$, coefficientwise, are exactly the time-one maps of such fields, and that the field is congruent to $g - \mathrm{id}$ modulo $p^{c+1}$. So the interpolated iterates of Bell and Poonen are flows of this kind, and I obtain a quantitative minimality criterion: if the displacements $g_i(x_0) - x_0$ of $d$ such maps span $p^k\mathbb{Z}_p^d$, the group they generate acts minimally on the ball of radius $p^{-k}$ about $x_0$. Where the argument of Cantat and Jang gives an orbit closure containing some open set, this names the ball, at every level $k$ and in every dimension; for $d = 2$ and $k = 1$ it is Jang's criterion for Markoff surfaces, which I test numerically at $7830$ points. Finally, the formal logarithm of $\mathbb{G}_m$ or of an elliptic curve is the rectifying coordinate of an explicit field, so the local divisibility $v_p([t]z) = v_p(z) + v_p(t)$ for $v_p(z) \ge 1 + c$, deep in the kernel of reduction, follows from the metric identity alone.

papers.title: Variational estimates for discrete spherical averages: $\ell^p$-boundedness and related arithmetic obstructions
papers.abstract: In this article, we investigate variational inequalities for the family of discrete spherical averages. We establish $\ell^p$-boundedness of the $r$-variation operators for $1<p<\infty$ and $r>2$ along sufficiently sparse sequences of factorial radii. Moreover, we also study arithmetic obstructions to these variational estimates and construct counterexamples to show that such boundedness properties for the corresponding variational operators cannot hold for lacunary sequences of radii.

papers.title: Cameron--Martin theorem for SLE welding measures
papers.abstract: For $\kappa\in(0,4]$, we prove a Cameron--Martin theorem for the welding law induced by SLE$_\kappa$ loop measure. Under simultaneous left and right composition $h\mapsto\varphi\circ h\circ\psi^{-1}$, the transformed law is mutually absolutely continuous with respect to the original law exactly when both maps belong to the Weil--Petersson group, and is mutually singular otherwise. Thus the Weil--Petersson group is the quasi-invariance group of the welding law under composition on either side. We also prove that it is its own normalizer in the group of orientation-preserving circle homeomorphisms. For Weil--Petersson pairs, we derive an explicit Radon--Nikodym derivative in terms of a relative action well defined for SLE weldings and prove that it belongs to $L^{1+\varepsilon}$ for some $\varepsilon>0$ depending on the pair.

papers.title: Character-Twisted Sums of Real Quadratic Class Numbers and a Selberg-Type Conjecture
papers.abstract: Extending the arithmetic Selberg-zeta function framework studied by Sarnak \cite{Sarnak1982} and Hashimoto \cite{Hashimoto2007}, we study Dirichlet-character weighted sums of narrow class numbers of real quadratic orders and derive explicit formulas according to the scalar, split, ramified, and inert reductions of primitive hyperbolic classes. Our first main result establishes asymptotic formulas for the class number sums associated with the three noninert reduction types and shows that, after multiplication by the corresponding nontrivial even-character weights, their leading terms cancel exactly for every fixed prime $p\ge 5$. Computational experiments across the sampled ranges of levels and geodesic lengths support a substantially stronger bound for the sum over nontrivial even-characters and exhibit systematic cancellation among the scalar, split, and ramified contributions. If this conjectural bound persists over arbitrarily long polynomial ranges, the resulting exceptional eigenvalues-free regions approach the Selberg threshold $1/4$, providing a possible arithmetic route toward a Selberg-type spectral gap.

papers.title: On Hilbert's tenth problem over a quadratic field
papers.abstract: In 2026, OpenAI proved that Hilbert's Tenth Problem over the field $\mathbb Q$ of rational numbers has a negative solution. In this paper we study Hilbert's Tenth Problem over the quadratic field $K=\mathbb Q(\sqrt2)$. We prove that there is no algorithm to decide for any polynomial equation $P(x_1,\ldots,x_{48})=0$ with integer coefficients whether it has solutions with $x_1,\ldots,x_{48}\in K$. We also show the existence of a polynomial $f(x_0,x_1,\ldots,x_{25})$ with integer coefficients such that $a\in K$ is a rational integer if and only if $f(a,x_1,\ldots,x_{25})=0$ for some $x_1,\ldots,x_{25}\in K$.

papers.title: Self-adjoint skew quartics, symplectic monodromy, and zeta functions
papers.abstract: For an odd prime power $P$, let $A_H(P)$ be the number of $a\in\F_{P^H}$ for which the self-adjoint skew quartic $t^4+t^3+at^2+t+1$ is irreducible in $\F_{P^H}[t;\sigma]$, with $\sigma(c)=c^P$. We determine $A_H(3)$ for every $H\ge1$ and prove that its minimal constant-coefficient recurrence has order $24$. Local ramification gives the degrees of the Steinberg and regular cuspidal Frobenius polynomials. Duality and finitely many exact counts determine both polynomials. For $P=p^f$ with $p\nmid f$, we construct an explicit genus-$P(P+1)/2$ flag curve whose zeta numerator is the Steinberg Frobenius polynomial. At $P=3$ this identifies the degree-$12$ factor computed above with the zeta numerator of a genus-$6$ curve. For general $P$ the flag curve and the regular cuspidal factors give a rational expression for the counting series. We evaluate the linear coefficients of the two factors by an elliptic-curve point count and express their quadratic coefficients through a single finite-field character sum.

papers.title: Arithmetic Upper and Lower Bounds for the Denumerant Function II
papers.abstract: We apply the elementary arithmetic argument of the first paper of this series (arXiv:2204.13689) to binomial coefficients, and obtain upper and lower bounds for Sylvester's denumerant function for arbitrary positive integers $a_1,\dots,a_k$ that sharpen those of Agnarsson. The lower bound is a sum of binomial coefficients; it holds along the multiples of $\gcd(a_1,\dots,a_k)$ without assuming that a solution exists, and it is greater than the polynomial lower bound of the first paper. In the upper bound the shift of Agnarsson's binomial coefficient is reduced.

papers.title: Algebraic independence of $v$-adic Carlitz multiple polylogarithms via period interpretations
papers.abstract: Based on Hartl's de Rham-crystalline comparison isomorphism, we formulate a notion of Andr\'{e}'s $v$-adic periods for a class of Anderson $\mathbb{F}_q[z]$-motives with respect to a degree-one finite place $v$ of a rational function field over a finite field, following Ancona-Fr\u{a}\c{t}il\u{a}'s formulation of $p$-adic periods. The formulation naturally produces deformation series of the resulting periods and Frobenius difference equations satisfied by these series. We then explain how the formulation brings the resulting $v$-adic periods within the scope of Chen's $v$-adic ABP criterion and of difference Galois theory, and gives us a strategy to study the transcendence degrees of $v$-adic periods through their deformation series. We show that certain special values of $v$-adic Carlitz multiple polylogarithms can be expressed in terms of Andr\'e's $v$-adic periods. Applying the strategy to these examples, we obtain algebraic independence results for certain special values of $v$-adic Carlitz multiple polylogarithms; more precisely, the transcendence degree of the field generated by a suitable collection of special values of $v$-adic Carlitz multiple polylogarithms is one less than the transcendence degree of the field generated by the corresponding special values of $\infty$-adic Carlitz multiple polylogarithms together with the Carlitz period.

papers.title: On the non-extendibility of triangular $D(n)$-pairs $\{n,2n\}$ with $n = 2k^2 \pm k$
papers.abstract: We study a class of Diophantine problems arising from triangular analogues of classical Diophantine tuples. A set of positive integers is called a triangular $D(n)$-tuple if the product of any two distinct elements, increased by $n$, is a triangular number. In this paper, we investigate the extensibility of triangular $D(n)$-pairs of the form $\{n,2n\}$, where $n = 2k^2 + \varepsilon k$, with $k$ an odd positive integer and $\varepsilon \in \{-1,1\}$ such that $4k + \varepsilon$ is prime. We prove that for all $(k,\varepsilon)$ in a finite explicitly determined set, the pair $\{n,2n\}$ cannot be extended to a triangular $D(n)$-quadruple. The obtained results give further evidence for a general non-extensibility phenomenon, which we formulate as a conjecture.

papers.title: Exceptional zeros for $\mathrm{GSp}(4) \times \mathrm{GL}(2)$ and Yoshida lifts
papers.abstract: The aim of this article is to study an exceptional zero phenomenon for the $p$-adic $L$-functions attached to $\mathrm{GSp}_4\times\mathrm{GL}_2$ in the critical regions (F) and (D). We construct improved $p$-adic $L$-functions by replacing the $p$-depleted Eisenstein family with its $p$-ordinary counterpart. Under a local compatibility hypothesis at the ramified places and classical control for the families, we show that their poles detect exactly the Yoshida lifts whose smaller constituent is dual to the $\mathrm{GL}_2$ representation. The proof compares their residues with distinguished automorphic periods, extending the coherent period formula to the case where one modular form has weight zero. An explicit Euler-factor identity relates each improved function to the usual $p$-adic $L$-function. At these Yoshida points, the vanishing factor cancels the pole, and the resulting value is expressed through the distinguished period and the logarithmic derivative of the ordinary elliptic root. We also discuss the expected factorization along Yoshida families into Hida--Rankin $p$-adic $L$-functions.

papers.title: Large Gaps Between Piatetski-Shapiro Primes
papers.abstract: A Piatetski-Shapiro prime is a prime number that can be written as $\lfloor m^c \rfloor$ for some positive integer $m$ and non-integer $c>1$. Li and Pan showed the results for small gaps between consecutive Piatetski-Shapiro primes for $1<c<9/8$. On the other hand, Deshouillers, Drmota, and M\"ullner showed the large gaps between Piatetski-Shapiro primes although they did not mention it explicitly whenever there are infinitely many Piatetski-Shapiro primes with exponent $c$ using binomial expansion. In this article, we use a different method from theirs, and we obtain the explicit exponent that appears in their paper.

papers.title: Arithmetic Upper and Lower Bounds for the Denumerant Function III
papers.abstract: We extend the denumerant to a weighted denumerant, the sum of a function $\mu$ over the solutions in non-negative integers of $a_1x_1+\cdots+a_kx_k=n$. For the monomial weights $x_1^{\alpha_1}\cdots x_k^{\alpha_k}$, with exponents $\alpha_i\in\mathbb{R}_{\geq0}$, we prove upper and lower bounds of the kind of those of the first paper of this series (arXiv:2204.13689), with an explicit constant and explicit shifts. As an example of application, summing these bounds over all the numbers $a_1,\dots,a_k$ we find, by elementary means, the asymptotic main term of the sums $\sum_{y_1+\cdots+y_k=n}\sigma_{\alpha_1}(y_1)\cdots\sigma_{\alpha_k}(y_k)$ of products of divisor functions, for every $k$ and for real exponents $\alpha_i\neq0$ of either sign.

papers.title: Note on the largest prime factors of consecutive integers II
papers.abstract: For an integer $n > 1$, let $P^+(n)$ be the largest prime factor of $n$. We show that a positive proportion of integers $n\leq x$ satisfy\begin{align*} P^+(n-1)<P^+(n)>P^+(n+1)<P^+(n+2)>P^+(n+3). \end{align*} The proof employs Selberg's upper-bound sieve and the multidimensional Selberg sieve developed in the Polymath8b work.

papers.title: The Riemann Hypothesis and Prime Numbers
papers.abstract: The Riemann hypothesis is attracting a great deal of attention at present. It is one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems in mathematics, for each of which the Clay Mathematics Institute offers a prize of one million dollars. It is arguably the most important open problem in all of mathematics. Numerous results have so far been proved only under the assumption of the Riemann hypothesis. Yet the hypothesis itself sounds rather dull: it conjectures that the zeros of a certain function have a certain form. Things become truly exciting, however, when we look at its connection with prime numbers, and that is what we shall do here.
